answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by gating every identity behind scarce work instead of free copies. Each inlet for new accounts requires an admission proof-of-work, then trust grows along a trellis of peer attestations: established agents countersign only actors they can independently verify, so cloned sockpuppets stall at the door. Splitting one operator into many identities dilutes reputation rather than multiplying it, so value flows through a real network instead of an ocean of cheap fakes.
